_meta.description: Curated, paraphrased clinical-practice-guideline recommendations for genitourinary cancers, used by LiteratureDB to anchor the search-page answer to official guidance alongside the retrieved primary literature.
_meta.disclaimer: These entries are short paraphrased summaries written for orientation, NOT verbatim reproductions of the guideline text. Most GU guideline texts are copyrighted (EAU) or licensed CC BY-NC-ND (ESMO / Onkopedia), so full text is not stored here. Always confirm wording, evidence level and currency against the linked official document. Research use only; not a substitute for clinical judgement.
_meta.how_to_extend: See README.md in this folder. Add objects to "recommendations"; each needs source, tumour, recommendation and url. Register any new issuing body under "sources".

recommendations.title: EAU Guidelines on Prostate Cancer
recommendations.recommendation: For low-risk localised prostate cancer, offer active surveillance rather than immediate radical prostatectomy or radiotherapy in patients with a life expectancy over 10 years.

recommendations.title: Prostate cancer: ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines
recommendations.recommendation: For high-risk / locally advanced localised prostate cancer, treat with radical radiotherapy combined with long-term androgen deprivation therapy, or radical prostatectomy with extended pelvic lymph-node dissection as part of multimodal management.

recommendations.title: Prostate cancer: ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines (metastatic hormone-sensitive)
recommendations.recommendation: In metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer, androgen deprivation therapy alone is not sufficient: combine it upfront with an androgen-receptor pathway inhibitor (abiraterone, apalutamide, enzalutamide or darolutamide). For fit patients with high-volume disease, an ADT + docetaxel + ARPI triplet is an option.

recommendations.title: Prostate cancer: ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines (mCRPC)
recommendations.recommendation: In metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer with a pathogenic BRCA1/BRCA2 (or other homologous-recombination-repair) alteration that has progressed on a new hormonal agent, offer a PARP inhibitor such as olaparib.

recommendations.title: EAU Guidelines on Prostate Cancer (mCRPC)
recommendations.recommendation: Offer 177Lu-PSMA-617 to patients with PSMA-positive metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who have progressed after at least one ARPI and taxane-based chemotherapy (or who are unfit for / decline chemotherapy).

recommendations.title: Germline and Somatic Genomic Testing for Metastatic Prostate Cancer: ASCO Guideline
recommendations.recommendation: Offer germline and somatic tumour testing for homologous-recombination-repair genes (including BRCA1/2, ATM, PALB2, CHEK2) and mismatch-repair deficiency / microsatellite instability to all patients with metastatic prostate cancer, to guide PARP-inhibitor and immunotherapy eligibility and cascade testing.

recommendations.title: EAU Guidelines on Prostate Cancer (supportive care)
recommendations.recommendation: In castration-resistant prostate cancer with bone metastases, offer a bone-protective agent (denosumab or zoledronic acid) to prevent skeletal-related events, with calcium and vitamin D supplementation and dental assessment.

recommendations.title: Interdisciplinary Swiss consensus recommendations on staging and treatment of advanced prostate cancer
recommendations.recommendation: PSMA-PET/CT is the preferred imaging modality for staging high-risk localised prostate cancer and for restaging biochemical recurrence, as it changes management in a substantial proportion of patients compared with conventional imaging.

recommendations.title: EAU Guidelines on Non-muscle-invasive Bladder Cancer
recommendations.recommendation: For high-risk non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer, perform a complete transurethral resection (with a second resection when indicated) followed by intravesical BCG induction plus 1–3 years of maintenance. Discuss early radical cystectomy for the highest-risk tumours.

recommendations.title: Bladder cancer: ESMO Clinical Practice Guideline
recommendations.recommendation: For muscle-invasive bladder cancer in cisplatin-eligible patients, give neoadjuvant cisplatin-based combination chemotherapy before radical cystectomy with pelvic lymph-node dissection.

recommendations.title: Bladder cancer: ESMO Clinical Practice Guideline (organ preservation)
recommendations.recommendation: Trimodality therapy – maximal transurethral resection followed by concurrent chemoradiotherapy – is an accepted bladder-preserving alternative to radical cystectomy in selected patients with organ-confined muscle-invasive disease and adequate bladder function.

recommendations.title: ESMO Clinical Practice Guideline interim update on first-line therapy in advanced urothelial carcinoma
recommendations.recommendation: Enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab is a preferred first-line option for locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma irrespective of cisplatin eligibility, having shown superior survival versus platinum-based chemotherapy.

recommendations.title: Bladder cancer: ESMO Clinical Practice Guideline (metastatic maintenance)
recommendations.recommendation: For metastatic urothelial carcinoma without progression after first-line platinum-based chemotherapy, give switch-maintenance avelumab (when enfortumab vedotin + pembrolizumab was not used first line).

recommendations.title: EAU Guidelines on Muscle-invasive and Metastatic Bladder Cancer (molecular testing)
recommendations.recommendation: Test for activating FGFR2/FGFR3 alterations in advanced urothelial carcinoma to identify candidates for erdafitinib after prior immunotherapy and platinum-based chemotherapy.

recommendations.title: EAU Guidelines on Renal Cell Carcinoma
recommendations.recommendation: For T1 renal tumours, offer nephron-sparing surgery (partial nephrectomy) in preference to radical nephrectomy whenever technically feasible. Active surveillance is an option for small renal masses in older patients or those with high comorbidity.

recommendations.title: Renal cell carcinoma: ESMO Clinical Practice Guideline (advanced)
recommendations.recommendation: First-line treatment of advanced clear-cell renal cell carcinoma is an immune-checkpoint-inhibitor-based combination – ipilimumab + nivolumab for IMDC intermediate/poor risk, or an ICI + tyrosine-kinase-inhibitor combination across risk groups.

recommendations.title: Renal cell carcinoma: ESMO Clinical Practice Guideline (adjuvant)
recommendations.recommendation: After nephrectomy for clear-cell renal cell carcinoma at increased risk of recurrence, adjuvant pembrolizumab for one year can be offered following a discussion of the disease-free-survival benefit against toxicity.

recommendations.title: Testicular seminoma and non-seminoma: ESMO-EURACAN Clinical Practice Guideline
recommendations.recommendation: After orchiectomy for stage I seminoma, active surveillance is the preferred management for most patients; single-agent carboplatin (one cycle) is an adjuvant alternative. Avoid routine adjuvant radiotherapy.

recommendations.title: Testicular germ-cell tumours: ESMO-EURACAN Clinical Practice Guideline (metastatic)
recommendations.recommendation: Treat metastatic germ-cell tumours with cisplatin-based combination chemotherapy (BEP) with the number of cycles set by the IGCCCG prognostic group, ideally at or in consultation with a high-volume centre.

recommendations.title: EAU-ASCO Collaborative Guideline on Penile Cancer
recommendations.recommendation: For localised penile cancer, use organ-sparing treatment where oncologically safe. Stage the inguinal nodes actively: sentinel-node biopsy or modified inguinal lymphadenectomy in clinically node-negative patients with intermediate-/high-risk primary tumours.

recommendations.title: Precision oncology – guideline of the Austrian, German and Swiss societies for haematology and medical oncology
recommendations.recommendation: In advanced genitourinary cancers, consider broad molecular profiling (including homologous-recombination-repair genes, microsatellite-instability / mismatch-repair status, tumour mutational burden and FGFR alterations) to identify targeted-therapy and immunotherapy options and clinical-trial eligibility, discussed in a molecular tumour board.
